sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: My biological father, who is Black, split when I was pretty young.
sentences.zh: 我的亲生父亲是黑人，在我很小的时候就离开了。

sentences.en: So I was raised by a single mother until I was about 10.
sentences.zh: 所以我由单亲妈妈抚养长大，直到我大约10岁。

sentences.en: My mother remarried to my adoptive father, who's a wonderful man.
sentences.zh: 我母亲改嫁给了我的养父，他是个非常好的人。

sentences.en: And just because we're about to be talking about affirmative action, Tyler, your mom, is she white?
sentences.zh: 而且既然我们马上要聊到平权法案，泰勒，你妈妈，她是白人吗？

sentences.en: She is, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，她是。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: My mother had a year or two of college, but had me very young, and finishing a four-year degree was not in the cards.
sentences.zh: 我母亲上过一两年大学，但很早就生了我，完成四年制学位是不可能的。

sentences.en: And I think she really wanted me to do what she hadn't been able to complete, which was a four-year college degree.
sentences.zh: 我想她真的很希望我能完成她没能做到的事情，那就是获得一个四年制大学学位。

sentences.en: So she was always really clear, hell or high water, I'd be going to college.
sentences.zh: 所以她一直态度非常明确，不管发生什么艰难险阻，我都必须上大学。

sentences.en: You'd be going to college.
sentences.zh: 你一定要上大学。

sentences.en: I was a curious student, I would say.
sentences.zh: 可以说我是一个好奇心很强的学生。

sentences.en: Not always the most motivated, I'll be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，并不总是最有积极性的。

sentences.en: I spent a lot of time fishing and playing guitar, but I did okay in terms of grades.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间钓鱼和弹吉他，但我的成绩还算过得去。

sentences.en: Like most high school students, I was required by the school to take the PSATs, the precursor
sentences.zh: 像大多数高中生一样，学校要求我参加PSAT考试，这是

sentences.en: to the SATs, and was very shocked to find when I got my results back that I had done really well.
sentences.zh: SAT考试的前身，当拿到成绩时我非常震惊，发现自己考得非常好。

sentences.en: And at that point, the guidance counselor and some other folks were telling me that I should think about a different caliber of institution than I think I previously had in mind.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，升学顾问和其他一些人告诉我，我应该考虑一个比我以前心目中更高水准的院校。

sentences.en: So I applied early decision to Haverford, and that was sort of all she wrote.
sentences.zh: 所以我提前决定申请了哈弗福德学院，事情基本上就这么定下来了。

sentences.en: So at the time that you applied to college, how did you identify yourself in terms of your race at that point?
sentences.zh: 在你申请大学的时候，你当时是如何认同自己的种族身份的？

sentences.en: I don't recall how I specifically checked boxes on my Haverford application form.
sentences.zh: 我不记得我在哈弗福德的申请表上具体勾选了哪些方框。

sentences.en: When available, I generally have checked black and white, if you can check both.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，如果可以勾选多个，我通常会同时勾选黑人和白人。

sentences.en: A lot of times, you can actually only check one.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，你实际上只能勾选一个。

sentences.en: In those cases, I've always, since I was young, just checked the black box.
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下，从小到大，我都只勾选黑人那一栏。

sentences.en: So you said you had excellent scores going into college, but was there an element of race as well?
sentences.zh: 所以你说你上大学时的成绩非常优秀，但其中是否也有种族因素？

sentences.en: Was affirmative action also at play there?
sentences.zh: 平权法案在其中也起作用了吗？

sentences.en: Do you have any sense of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么感觉吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember really clearly in my Haverford interview, where the interviewer was asking me about my hobbies, and I mentioned I used to do competitive bass fishing tournaments
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得很清楚，在我的哈弗福德面试中，面试官问我有什么爱好，我提到我曾参加过竞技黑鲈钓鱼比赛，

sentences.en: really seriously all over the NortheaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且在整个东北地区都很认真地参加。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so I was actually, to my knowledge, the youngest person to go to the state championship when I was 16.
sentences.zh: 是的，据我所知，我在16岁时是参加州锦标赛年龄最小的人。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And she thought that was delightful, but she said a number of things along the lines of, that's a curious hobby for someone of your background.
sentences.zh: 她觉得这很有趣，但她说了一些类似于“对于你这种背景的人来说，这是一个奇怪的爱好”这样的话。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I didn't really know what she meant by my background, because I'm from an area where a lot of people fish, so I thought I had the exact background for someone who would do
sentences.zh: 我当时并不太明白她说的“我的背景”是什么意思，因为我来自一个很多人钓鱼的地区，所以我认为我完全具备会做

sentences.en: this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 这种事的人的背景。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I gradually came to realize she meant my racial background.
sentences.zh: 我渐渐意识到她指的是我的种族背景。

sentences.en: A Black fisherman was not something they ran into a lot.
sentences.zh: 一个黑人渔夫并不是他们经常遇到的事情。

sentences.en: And she really fixated on that, asked me a ton of questions about it, and I think it was one of the reasons they were interested in me.
sentences.zh: 她真的很执着于这一点，问了我一大堆关于这方面的问题，我想这也是他们对感兴趣的原因之一。

sentences.en: She thought I had a curious background, she kept saying.
sentences.zh: 她一直说，她觉得我的背景很奇特。

sentences.en: Based on the tone of my conversation with the admissions officer, it was very clear to me that they were very excited to be talking to a person of color, especially a person of
sentences.zh: 根据我和招生官员谈话的语气，我很清楚地看出，他们非常高兴能和一个有色人种交谈，特别是和一个让他们感到兴奋的、成绩很好的

sentences.en: color that had scores they were excited about.
sentences.zh: 有色人种交谈。

sentences.en: Well, how did that make you feel?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这让你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: What did you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你对此是怎么想的？

sentences.en: I've always had mixed feelings about affirmative action, very grateful for it.
sentences.zh: 我对平权法案一直有着复杂的情感，非常感激它。

sentences.en: I think it's important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: I think it's necessary.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是必要的。

sentences.en: But it's also just uncomfortable to realize you are somewhere, whether you deserve to be there or not, because of the color of your skin.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅因为你的肤色而意识到自己身处某地（无论你是否配得上那里），也是一种不舒服的感觉。

sentences.en: As I left Haverford and went on to my PhD program, I began tutoring the first summer after grad school as a way to make extra money during the summers.
sentences.zh: 当我离开哈弗福德去读博士项目时，研究生毕业后的那个夏天我开始做家教，以此作为夏天赚取额外收入的一种方式。

sentences.en: And it was really once I started tutoring that I became fully aware of the extent to which
sentences.zh: 正是从我开始做家教开始，我才真正充分意识到

sentences.en: affirmative action seemed to have gone off the rails in really problematic and quite disturbing directions.
sentences.zh: 平权法案似乎已经在非常 проблематичный（有问题）且相当令人不安的方向上脱轨了。

sentences.en: You know, I was somebody getting a literature PhD.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我是一个攻读文学博士学位的人。

sentences.en: My bread and butter was helping them with their writing and their college essay in particular.
sentences.zh: 我的核心工作是帮他们提高写作能力，尤其是他们的大学申请论文。

sentences.en: And I came to realize very swiftly that this intense concern about leveraging, minimizing, or
sentences.zh: 我很快意识到，这种对如何利用、淡化或

sentences.en: maximizing one's identity in ways that would be legible and beneficial in the admissions process was something most of these students seem to have in mind.
sentences.zh: 最大化自己的身份以使其在招生过程中清晰可见并带来利益的强烈关注，似乎是大多数这些学生心中所想的事情。

sentences.en: Do you remember, Tyler, the first time you started encountering this?
sentences.zh: 泰勒，你还记得你第一次遇到这种情况是什么时候吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然记得。

sentences.en: The first student I encountered who had this mindset was a Chinese-American student who I tutored in Queens.
sentences.zh: 我遇到的第一个有这种心态的学生是我在皇后区辅导的一名华裔美国学生。

sentences.en: And I arrived and she has all her materials.
sentences.zh: 我到了那里，她准备好了所有的材料。

sentences.en: And she wanted me to look through them.
sentences.zh: 她想让我过目一下。

sentences.en: And she asked me to read them to make sure they didn't seem too Asian.
sentences.zh: 她让我读一读，以确保它们看起来不会太“亚洲化”。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: And I laughed because I thought she was being ironic.
sentences.zh: 我笑了，因为我以为她在开玩笑。

sentences.en: And she was like, no, I'm serious.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，我是认真的。

sentences.en: And she pulled out her CV and was like, I've been wondering, can I keep chess and math club on here or do those seem too Asian?
sentences.zh: 她拿出了自己的简历说，我一直在想，我能把国际象棋和数学俱乐部留在上面吗，还是说这些看起来太亚洲化了？

sentences.en: Like, are those too stereotypical?
sentences.zh: 就像是，这些是不是太刻板印象了？

sentences.en: And so we ended up having like a 20-minute conversation about whether or not chess and math club are too stereotypically Asian to put on her CV or if it would actually be better
sentences.zh: 所以我们最终花了大约20分钟讨论国际象棋和数学俱乐部是否带有太多刻板的亚洲色彩，不适合写进简历，或者对她来说

sentences.en: for her just not to mention that she had done those.
sentences.zh: 干脆不提她参加过这些活动会更好。

sentences.en: I thought it was kind of odd, very sad, a little strange, and slightly amusing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点反常，非常悲哀，有点奇怪，还有点滑稽。

sentences.en: I thought this would be a one-off kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我以为这只是一次性的事情。

sentences.en: But these kinds of conversations were basically the norm throughout my tutoring.
sentences.zh: 但这类对话基本上贯穿了我整个家教生涯的常态。

sentences.en: And these were not cynically conspiring students that desperately were just trying to rig the system.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是那些绝望地想要操纵体制的愤世嫉俗的阴谋家学生。

sentences.en: It was very clear to me that they felt that this is what was expected of them.
sentences.zh: 我很清楚地感觉到，他们觉得这就是别人对他们的期望。

sentences.en: This is what was wanted from them.
sentences.zh: 这就是别人希望从他们身上看到的。

sentences.en: And they were just trying to do it as best they could.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在尽最大努力去做到这一点。

sentences.en: So the Supreme Court hands down the ruling that overturns affirmative action.
sentences.zh: 所以最高法院下达了推翻平权法案的裁决。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: What was the first thing that came to your mind?
sentences.zh: 你脑子里闪过的第一件事是什么？

sentences.en: I think what I thought is that things are just going to get worse.
sentences.zh: 我想我的想法是事情只会变得更糟。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think there's going to be some efforts to figure out ways to maintain the current level of diversity in ways that are compliant with the law.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我认为将会出现一些努力，去寻找在符合法律的情况下维持当前多元化水平的方法。

sentences.en: I think some institutions will do this.
sentences.zh: 我认为一些机构会这么做。

sentences.en: I think I work at an institution that will do this.
sentences.zh: 我认为我工作的机构就会这么做。

sentences.en: But I think a lot of the negative externalities of affirmative action are going to get worse.
sentences.zh: 但我认为平权法案带来的许多负面外部效应会变得更糟。

sentences.en: And get worse how, Tyler?
sentences.zh: 泰勒，怎么个更糟法？

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊这个。

sentences.en: I think it leads to an atmosphere in which race and value are deeply intertwined in these students' consciousness as they're entering these institutions.
sentences.zh: 我认为这导致了一种氛围，当这些学生进入这些机构时，种族和价值在他们的意识中深度交织在一起。

sentences.en: And I don't know that that leaves once they're there.
sentences.zh: 而且我不知道他们到了那里之后这种想法会不会消失。

sentences.en: And why does the decision, though, make that more the case?
sentences.zh: 但是，为什么这个裁决会让这种情况更加严重呢？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Because colleges are still going to want to diversify.
sentences.zh: 因为大学仍然希望实现多元化。

sentences.en: And the options they're going to have for identifying diverse students is going to be through the prism of the college essay.
sentences.zh: 他们用来识别多元化学生的选择将通过大学申请论文的棱镜来进行。

sentences.en: There are not going to be some of the other mechanisms available to identify students of color.
sentences.zh: 将不会有一些其他可用的机制来识别有色人种学生。

sentences.en: And so students of color are going to be forced to or feel compelled to lean more caricaturishly into their racial identity, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，有色人种学生将被迫或感到被迫更加夸张地倾向于他们的种族身份，对吧？

sentences.en: And to present, you know, versions of their racial identity that will be the most legible to admissions officers.
sentences.zh: 并且，你知道的，呈现出对招生官员来说最容易理解的种族身份版本。

sentences.en: Other students might find creative ways to be racially ambiguous, right?
sentences.zh: 其他学生可能会找到创造性的方法来变得种族模糊，对吧？

sentences.en: Make it a little harder for colleges to read, you know, what someone's racial identity might be.
sentences.zh: 让大学更难读懂某人的种族身份可能是什么。

sentences.en: I mean, that's my prediction, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的预测就是这样，是的。

sentences.en: I think we're going to be left with all of the negative externalities of affirmative action without the benefits of actual structural redress and opportunity that accompanied a
sentences.zh: 我认为我们最终将不得不承受平权法案带来的所有负面外部效应，却享受不到伴随着一个不可否认但比替代方案更好的系统而来的实际结构性纠正和机遇的好处。

sentences.en: system that was admittedly imperfect, but better than the alternative.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 他们对你有什么期望？

sentences.en: So, a lot of expectations were placed upon me at an early age to be a gifted child, to study hard, and definitely to attend an elite college.
sentences.zh: 所以，我很小的时候就被寄予厚望，要当一个天才儿童，努力学习，而且绝对要考上一流名校。

sentences.en: And that was always the priority.
sentences.zh: 这始终是重中之重。

sentences.en: My mom used state school as a threat.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈把普通公立大学当成一种威胁。

sentences.en: She'd say, like, you're either going to an Ivy or Rutgers.
sentences.zh: 她会说，你要么去常春藤盟校，要么去罗格斯大学。

sentences.en: There's no in-between.
sentences.zh: 没有中间选择。

sentences.en: I'm not paying for your tuition if you don't get into an Ivy.
sentences.zh: 如果你考不上常春藤，我是不会给你付学费的。

sentences.en: GPA was always firSt.
sentences.zh: GPA永远是第一位的。

sentences.en: That was just the kind of pressure I grew up under.
sentences.zh: 我就是在这种压力下长大的。

sentences.en: And it made me feel like my self-worth was tied to a school or tied to my results, even though that's completely not the case.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得我的自我价值与学校或考试结果挂钩，尽管事实完全不是这样。

sentences.en: What do you think was behind your mom emphasizing elite schools in particular, you know, Ivy
sentences.zh: 你觉得你妈妈为什么特别强调名校，比如说常春藤

sentences.en: League schools?
sentences.zh: 联盟的学校？

sentences.en: What was she trying to say there?
sentences.zh: 她当时是想表达什么意思？

sentences.en: I think she was saying this coming out from her own lived experiences and insecurities and the hardships that she's been through.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她是结合了她自己的人生经历、不安全感以及她所经历的艰难困苦才有感而发的。

sentences.en: She honestly, like, works harder than anyone else I know.
sentences.zh: 说实话，她比我认识的任何人都努力。

sentences.en: She can't go out because she's working.
sentences.zh: 她不能出去玩，因为她要工作。

sentences.en: And if she's not working, she's taking care of me or my brother, or she's giving rides, or she's cooking.
sentences.zh: 如果不工作，她就要照顾我和我弟弟，或者开车送人，或者做饭。

sentences.en: So, she never really had a life outside of her work and her family.
sentences.zh: 所以，除了工作和家庭，她基本上没有什么个人的生活。

sentences.en: And she thought that me having an elite education at an elite institution meant that it would unlock a lot more opportunities.
sentences.zh: 她认为让我在一所顶尖名校接受一流教育，意味着能解锁更多的机会。

sentences.en: And in the end, it comes down to money.
sentences.zh: 说到底，这还是归结于钱的问题。

sentences.en: She didn't want me to be tied down to just working, working, working, just like she did.
sentences.zh: 她不想让我像她那样，被没完没了的工作彻底绑死。

sentences.en: But rather, she wanted me to have financial freedom.
sentences.zh: 相反，她希望我能获得财务自由。

sentences.en: She wanted me to have the freedom to pursue what I'm passionate about.
sentences.zh: 她希望我有自由去追求自己真正热爱的事物。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, I think that's a very noble dream.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，我觉得这是一个非常崇高的梦想。

sentences.en: It's very selfless.
sentences.zh: 非常无私。

sentences.en: But that's kind of why she pushed me so hard to achieve success at an Ivy League institution.
sentences.zh: 但这也就是为什么她那么拼命地逼我，希望我能考进常春藤盟校取得成功。

sentences.en: So, tell me about your high school experience.
sentences.zh: 那么，跟聊聊你的高中经历吧。

sentences.en: What was it like at high school?
sentences.zh: 你在高中的生活是怎样的？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, throughout high school, I was very ambitious as a student.
sentences.zh: 嗯，整个高中期间，作为学生我都非常有上进心。

sentences.en: And I was very dedicated and committed to extracurriculars.
sentences.zh: 而且我对课外活动非常投入且执着。

sentences.en: What's an example, Gia?
sentences.zh: 能举个例子吗，吉娅？

sentences.en: Tell me what you did.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说你都做了什么。

sentences.en: So, for two years, I worked as co-editor-in-chief for my newspaper and my school's literary magazine.
sentences.zh: 有两年时间，我担任校报和学校文学杂志的联合主编。

sentences.en: I self-published a book talking about the different challenges that we as Gen Z face, created a nonprofit organization for youth mental health.
sentences.zh: 我自费出版了一本书，探讨我们Z世代面临的各种挑战，还创立了一个关注青少年心理健康的非营利组织。

sentences.en: I did varsity chair and martial arts.
sentences.zh: 我是校队队长，还练过武术。

sentences.en: I also played the violin.
sentences.zh: 我还拉小提琴。

sentences.en: I've been playing for 12 years now.
sentences.zh: 我已经练了12年了。

sentences.en: I was the concertmaster of my school's orchestra.
sentences.zh: 我是学校管弦乐团的首席。

sentences.en: I had a 4.56 GPA.
sentences.zh: 我的GPA是4.56。

sentences.en: And after my junior year, I attended a creative writing summer program at University of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 在高三结束后，我参加了宾夕法尼亚大学的创意写作夏令营。

sentences.en: I loved just all the instructors and the assignments, connected so well with the people, loved the culture.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢那里所有的导师和作业了，和大家相处得非常好，也很喜欢那种文化氛围。

sentences.en: For me, UPenn felt like somewhere that I could call home.
sentences.zh: 对当时的我觉得，宾大就像是一个我可以称之为家的地方。

sentences.en: So, I applied early decision there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在提前批（Early Decision）阶段申请了那里。

sentences.en: And the day before my decision came out, people around me were saying, like, oh, you are going to get...
sentences.zh: 就在放榜的前一天，我身边的人都在说，哦，你肯定能……

sentences.en: Like, they were already making their Instagram stories, posts, to, like, say, like, yeah, you got in.
sentences.zh: 比如说，他们甚至都已经做好了Instagram快拍和帖子，就等着发出来庆祝你被录取了。

sentences.en: My friends were like, they had cake prepared.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友们甚至还准备好了蛋糕。

sentences.en: They had all these things prepared.
sentences.zh: 他们把所有这些庆祝的东西都准备好了。

sentences.en: But they said, if you don't get in, who is gonna?
sentences.zh: 但他们说，如果你都考不上，那还有谁能考上？

sentences.en: Like, who's going to get in?
sentences.zh: 就像是，还有谁能进得去？

sentences.en: So, it was kind of like a no-brainer that I would go to, not even just an Ivy, but at least a top 20, an elite institution.
sentences.zh: 所以大家觉得我去读大学是十拿九稳的事，而且不只是常春藤，至少也得是前二十名的顶尖名校。

sentences.en: Overall, that day, I was, like, so nervous.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，那天我紧张得要命。

sentences.en: I couldn't eat.
sentences.zh: 我根本吃不下饭。

sentences.en: I could barely sleep that night, too.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上我也几乎没怎么合眼。

sentences.en: And when it was time for me to open my decision, my family was behind me, looking at my laptop.
sentences.zh: 到了要查录取结果的时候，我的家人都站在我身后，盯着我的笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: They were all excited to check.
sentences.zh: 他们都兴奋地等着查看结果。

sentences.en: And then it was 7 p.m.
sentences.zh: 本来结果应该在晚上7点公布。

sentences.en: when decisions were supposed to come out.
sentences.zh: 我还记得结果出来时已经是7点02分了，因为我又多等了整整两分钟。

sentences.en: I still remember it was 7.02 when it came out because I had to wait two whole minutes.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像过了一个世纪那么漫长。

sentences.en: Which felt like forever.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像过了一个世纪那么漫长。

sentences.en: But when I opened my letter, it said, like, sorry, we regret to inform you, dot, dot, dot.
sentences.zh: 但当我打开录取信时，上面写着，非常遗憾，我们很抱歉地通知您，省略号。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And that was not even a possibility in my mind, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这在我脑海里根本就是不可能发生的事。

sentences.en: I think that was probably the biggest shock of my life.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是我人生中受到的最大打击。

sentences.en: I mean, I've only lived 18 years, but it was still a huge shock for me and my family, you know?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我才活了18年，但这对我和我的家庭来说仍然是个巨大的打击，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I got rejected, not even deferred.
sentences.zh: 但我被拒绝了，甚至连延期录取（Deferred）都不是。

sentences.en: And what happened?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: What did you do?
sentences.zh: 你做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, after that, I was just still in shock.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那之后，我还处于震惊之中。

sentences.en: I wasn't really feeling anything.
sentences.zh: 其实没什么特别的感觉。

sentences.en: I was really numb.
sentences.zh: 整个人都麻木了。

sentences.en: But I was also so upset that I didn't even know how to react.
sentences.zh: 但我又气愤得甚至不知道该怎么反应。

sentences.en: But I decided to just stay up all night working on my other applications for my other schools.
sentences.zh: 不过我决定通宵不睡，继续完善其他学校的申请材料。

sentences.en: And I added a bunch more to my college list because I was scared that if this is how it's going to play out,
sentences.zh: 而且我在申请名单里又加了好几所大学，因为我害怕如果接下来事情都这样发展的话，

sentences.en: then I better try out everything possible and give my all to all of these schools instead of attaching my dream to one school.
sentences.zh: 那我还不如尝试所有可能的途径，把全部心血倾注在这些学校上，而不是把梦想全押在一所学校身上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: But I had never expected anything like this to be my reality.
sentences.zh: 但我从来没想过这种事会变成现实。

sentences.en: And no one had an explanation for why.
sentences.zh: 而且对于原因，谁也给不出一个解释。

sentences.en: Like, we couldn't attribute it to anything.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我们根本找不到任何归咎的理由。

sentences.en: I just felt really horrible about myself.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得自己糟糕透了。

sentences.en: I felt like I couldn't really show my face really in public.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己简直没脸在公众场合露面。

sentences.en: Like, I felt ashamed.
sentences.zh: 就觉得很羞耻。

sentences.en: Like, I was having this big sticker in my head that said, like, loser, I didn't make it.
sentences.zh: 感觉自己脑门上贴着一个巨大的标签，上面写着“失败者，你没考上”。

sentences.en: But my mom also said that she couldn't meet with her friends.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈也说她没法去见她的朋友们。

sentences.en: She felt embarrassed, too.
sentences.zh: 她也觉得很丢脸。

sentences.en: And I totally understood because in my community, there's also a culture of a lot of gossip and seeing if your kids didn't turn out this way,
sentences.zh: 我完全理解，因为在我们这个社群里，也有很多八卦的文化，总会看着如果你的孩子没有怎样怎样，

sentences.en: then it means you didn't really succeed as maybe a parent or something went wrong.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着你作为父母没有真正成功，或者哪里出了问题。

sentences.en: Like, what went wrong there?
sentences.zh: 就像是，到底是哪里出问题了？

sentences.en: In the days and weeks after you got your admissions decisions, what were your family members and friends and community members saying to you?
sentences.zh: 在收到大学录取结果后的几天和几周里，你的家人、朋友和社区里的人都是怎么对你说的？

sentences.en: One thing that kind of stood out to me was people said you just got affirmative action, like as a verb.
sentences.zh: 有件事让我印象深刻，有人说“你只是中了平权法案的招”，把平权法案当动词用。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: What did that mean, you just got affirmative action?
sentences.zh: “你只是中了平权法案的招”是什么意思？

sentences.en: It was people telling me that I was disadvantaged because of affirmative action in my race.
sentences.zh: 大家是在对我说，因为平权法案和我的族裔，我处于不利地位。

sentences.en: It was people talking about the race box and how big of a deal it was.
sentences.zh: 大家都在讨论申请表上的族裔勾选项，以及这到底有多大影响。

sentences.en: That's what people have said either as a joke or a passing comment.
sentences.zh: 人们要么当成笑话，要么随口一提，就是这么说的。

sentences.en: So just thinking about all of this was kind of what informed my beliefs about affirmative action at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以回想这一切，正是这些言论在当时塑造了我对平权法案的看法。

sentences.en: And Gia, what was going through your mind when you heard that the Supreme Court had overturned affirmative action?
sentences.zh: 吉娅，当你听到最高法院推翻平权法案的消息时，你心里在想些什么？

sentences.en: It was actually a lot of conflicting emotions initially.
sentences.zh: 起初其实交织着许多矛盾的情绪。

sentences.en: Part of me was, like, very happy that this would be the future.
sentences.zh: 我有一部分内心甚至感到很高兴，觉得未来会是这样。

sentences.en: Also, part of me was feeling bitter because I felt like I was wronged in some senses or screwed over.
sentences.zh: 但另一部分又感到愤愤不平，因为我觉得自己在某种意义上受到了不公正对待或者被坑了。

sentences.en: As a lot of people were buzzing around me saying, if you just applied a year later, you'd end up at an illy institution.
sentences.zh: 因为我身边有很多人都在议论纷纷，说如果你要是晚一年申请，就能进名校了。

sentences.en: But also, I want to say that my view changed since then.
sentences.zh: 不过我也想说，从那以后我的看法改变了。

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这方面的转变吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of Asian Americans wanted affirmative action to be overturned.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很多亚裔美国人都希望推翻平权法案。

sentences.en: But then on my social media feeds, I was seeing a lot of discourse, a lot of the side that I wasn't really familiar with.
sentences.zh: 但后来在我的社交媒体上，我看到了大量的讨论，接触到了很多我以前并不太熟悉的立场。

sentences.en: And that was Asian Americans for affirmative action.
sentences.zh: 也就是“支持平权法案的亚裔美国人”的声音。

sentences.en: And I was thinking, is my opinion wrong?
sentences.zh: 当时我就在想，难道我的观点错了吗？

sentences.en: Like, am I misreading something?
sentences.zh: 我是不是哪里会错了意？

sentences.en: And after I've consumed some media and talking to a few people who have differing opinions about affirmative action,
sentences.zh: 在看了一些相关报道并和几个对平权法案持不同意见的人交谈之后，

sentences.en: one thing that I mainly agree with is that I think the misconception within the Asian American community is that our spots are being taken away by Black and brown students and those minorities,
sentences.zh: 我比较赞同的一个观点是，亚裔美国人群体中存在一个误解，认为我们的名额是被黑人和棕色人种学生以及其他少数族裔抢走了，

sentences.en: although they only make up a very tiny percentage of actual population in classrooms in elite colleges like Harvard.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们在哈佛等精英高校的实际课堂人口中所占比例其实非常小。

sentences.en: And in this Supreme Court decision, it seems like Asian people are being pitted against Black and brown minorities,
sentences.zh: 而且在这次最高法院的裁决中，似乎把亚裔和黑人及棕色人种少数族裔对立了起来，

sentences.en: but that conveniently ignores the fact that legacy and trust fund and donations on all those things exiSt.
sentences.zh: 但这却刻意忽视了一个事实，那就是校友子弟照顾（legacy）、信托基金和巨额捐赠这些东西一直都存在。

sentences.en: And even though that's not the focus of the case, it still is like the underlying major player at hand that is being ignored.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并不是案件的焦点，但它依然是那个被忽视的、在背后起决定性作用的主要因素。

sentences.en: So there's a misunderstanding in the Asian American community about the culprit.
sentences.zh: 所以亚裔美国人群体对真正的“罪魁祸首”存在误解。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what exactly is your position on race conscious admissions policies now?
sentences.zh: 那你现在对照顾族裔多元化的招生政策到底是什么立场？

sentences.en: How would you describe it?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么描述它？

sentences.en: Can I not answer this?
sentences.zh: 我能不回答这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Because I'm not exactly sure yet.
sentences.zh: 因为我还没完全想清楚。

sentences.en: So I'm like trying to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 所以我还在试图理清头绪。

sentences.en: I can't say for certain, like whether I'm one side or the other.
sentences.zh: 我没法确定地说自己到底是站在哪一边。

sentences.en: I still have like feelings of both sides kind of just mixed all together.
sentences.zh: 我内心依然混杂着双方的各种感受，全都揉成了一团。

sentences.en: Could you talk through some of the uncertainties?
sentences.zh: 你能聊聊让你感到不确定的地方吗？

sentences.en: Because I think that's a very natural reaction, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这也是一种很自然的反应，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a complicated thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件很复杂的事情。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of different groups with different views on it as you've laid out.
sentences.zh: 正如你所梳理的，有很多不同的群体对此持有不同的看法。

sentences.en: I mean, is there something that you're grappling with?
sentences.zh: 我是说，有什么事情是你一直在纠结的吗？

sentences.en: So part of me, especially initially, feels like my results could be different if I was applying in the next admission cycle.
sentences.zh: 所以我的内心有一部分，特别是一开始的时候，总觉得如果我在下一届招生季申请，结果可能会不一样。

sentences.en: But also like majority of me and another part of me feels like, you know, that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 但我的大部分理智和另一部分直觉又觉得，你知道的，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Let's be real.
sentences.zh: 说实话。

sentences.en: It's not just about race.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关乎族裔。

sentences.en: It's about so many other factors.
sentences.zh: 这里面涉及太多其他的因素了。

sentences.en: And it makes me feel frustrated that I can't attribute one thing to all of my rejections in the way that my college results played out.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到很沮丧，因为我无法把所有的申请被拒以及最终的结果简单归咎于某一个单一原因。

sentences.en: Because like there are so many other underlying factors that are not revealed.
sentences.zh: 因为还有太多其他未曾公开的深层因素。

sentences.en: So I can't say for certain that it was my race that didn't get me into these schools.
sentences.zh: 所以我无法确切地说，就是因为我的族裔才导致我没能考上这些学校。

sentences.en: But part of me feels like it did play a role.
sentences.zh: 但我的直觉又觉得这确实起到了一定作用。

sentences.en: However, I also am sympathetic to the argument.
sentences.zh: 不过，我也对那种观点表示理解。

sentences.en: And I very much agree with the argument that we still need to have diverse classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 我非常赞同这样一种论点，即我们仍然需要保持校园的多元化。

sentences.en: We still need to maintain race conscious acceptances.
sentences.zh: 我们依然需要维持考量族裔因素的招生录取政策。

sentences.en: And I think that the Supreme Court case ruling was also not to make admissions colorblind.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为最高法院的判决也不是为了让招生过程对种族视而不见。

sentences.en: Like in reality, we still have so many other things like legacy and recruited athletes that are still being given an advantage.
sentences.zh: 现实中，我们依然有校友子弟照顾和特长生照顾等诸多享有优势的潜规则。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, that harms Asian Americans, too.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这也同样在伤害着亚裔美国人。

sentences.en: And that's what I believe.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的看法。

sentences.en: How do you feel about starting Boston University in the fall?
sentences.zh: 你对即将在秋季入读波士顿大学有什么感觉？

sentences.en: There's a lot of nervous energy, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，大家都有一种焦虑的情绪。

sentences.en: I'm, of course, very excited to start.
sentences.zh: 我当然非常高兴能开始大学生活。

sentences.en: I'm excited to take classes that I want to take and have opportunities that I didn't have in high school.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能选修自己想上的课程，并获得在高中时没有的机会。

sentences.en: But I also feel like this is not in any way an indicator of my potential.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得，这在任何方面都不能说明我的潜力。

sentences.en: It's just a matter of like what I make of the college experience.
sentences.zh: 这只在于我如何看待和利用大学经历。

sentences.en: How does your mom feel about you going to Boston University?
sentences.zh: 你妈妈对你去波士顿大学上学有什么看法？

sentences.en: Now she feels very proud, actually.
sentences.zh: 现在她其实感到非常骄傲。

sentences.en: Like Boston University is something to be so grateful for.
sentences.zh: 就好像能去波士顿大学是一件特别值得感恩的事。

sentences.en: And the tuition thing is, it's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 至于学费问题，那完全不是个事儿。

sentences.en: Like she is 100 percent willing to support me.
sentences.zh: 她百分之百愿意支持我。

sentences.en: She still has some dreams for me and some expectations for me.
sentences.zh: 她对我依然有一些梦想和期望。

sentences.en: Like she wants me to go to grad school.
sentences.zh: 比如她希望我去读研究生。

sentences.en: But it's more like what is the person that I will become in college?
sentences.zh: 但比起这个，她更关心我在大学里会成长为一个什么样的人。

sentences.en: And not so much like what is her dream that I will achieve, you know?
sentences.zh: 而不是去实现她的什么梦想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, to that point, Gia, your mom had really valued these elite schools, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说到这儿，吉娅，你妈妈以前真的很看重这些精英学校，对吧？

sentences.en: And now she's saying what matters is who you become as a person.
sentences.zh: 而现在她说，最重要的反而是你作为一个人的成长。

sentences.en: What has changed her viewpoint on all of this?
sentences.zh: 是什么改变了她对这一切的看法？

sentences.en: I think it's just realizing that college admissions is very arbitrary nowadays to the point where
sentences.zh: 我想只是因为她意识到，如今的大学招生非常随性，甚至到了

sentences.en: it's almost comical how my results turned out because not a single person I can think of would have expected this from me.
sentences.zh: 我的录取结果出来时简直有点滑稽，因为我想象不出会有哪怕一个人预料到会是这样。

sentences.en: And foundationally, like putting up all of our dreams and all of our goals into a school is very silly as well.
sentences.zh: 而且从根本上讲，把我们所有的梦想和目标全都押在一所学校上，也是很傻的做法。

sentences.en: So I'm very happy that I'm of the person who I've become throughout high school and the person that I am today.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴，我成为了高中三年成长起来的那个自己，也成为了今天的我。

sentences.en: And my parents also know that going on, I'll make the most of my resources and environment.
sentences.zh: 我的父母也很清楚，接下来我会充分利用所有的资源和环境。

sentences.en: And I don't see your school name as an indicator of success or anything to indicate your self-worth.
sentences.zh: 我并不认为学校的名字能说明成功，或者能代表你的自我价值。

sentences.en: Well, Gia, I really, really thank you for taking the time to talk to me.
sentences.zh: 好的，吉娅，非常非常感谢你抽空和我聊天。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And congratulations about getting into BU and good luck there.
sentences.zh: 恭喜你考入波士顿大学，祝你在那里一切都好。

sentences.en: It's a really, really good school.
sentences.zh: 那真的是一所非常非常好的学校。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你百忙之中接受采访。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: NATO is stronger, more energized, and yes, more united than ever in its history.
sentences.zh: 北约比以往任何时候都更加强大、更有活力，是的，也更加团结。

sentences.en: Indeed, more vital to our shared future.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对我们共同的未来至关重要。

sentences.en: It didn't happen by accident.
sentences.zh: 这不是偶然发生的。

sentences.en: It wasn't inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这不是不可避免的。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, members of NATO concluded their two-day summit in Lithuania, pledging unity in their support for Ukraine, but declining to invite the country in to the alliance.
sentences.zh: 周三，北约成员国在立陶宛结束了为期两天的峰会，承诺团结一致支持乌克兰，但拒绝邀请该国加入北约。

sentences.en: NATO leaders said that Ukraine, quote, belonged in NATO, but they refused to spell out when or how Ukraine would eventually become a member.
sentences.zh: 北约领导人表示，乌克兰“属于北约”，但他们拒绝明确乌克兰最终何时或如何成为成员。

sentences.en: And inflation slowed significantly in June, with the consumer price index climbing 3%, far below its 9% peak last summer.
sentences.zh: 6月通胀显著放缓，消费者价格指数（CPI）上涨3%，远低于去年夏天9%的峰值。

sentences.en: The numbers offered some of the most hopeful news for consumers since the Federal Reserve started trying to rein in price increases 16 months ago.
sentences.zh: 这些数据为消费者带来了一年多来美联储开始试图遏制物价上涨以来最充满希望的消息之一。

sentences.en: They were also a potential sign that the economy might yet avoid a recession.
sentences.zh: 这也可能是一个信号，表明经济或许仍能避免衰退。

sentences.en: Finally, Milan Kundera, the Czech-born French author, who became one of the most influential figures of 20th century literature, died on Tuesday in his home in Paris.
sentences.zh: 最后，捷克裔法国作家、20世纪文学最具影响力的人物之一米兰·昆德拉于周二在巴黎家中逝世。

sentences.en: He was 94.
sentences.zh: 享年94岁。

sentences.en: His best-known work was his 1984 novel,
sentences.zh: 他最著名的作品是1984年的小说

sentences.en: The Unbearable Lightness of Being.
sentences.zh: 《不能承受的生命之轻》。

sentences.en: He won fame for depicting oppression in Central Europe under communist rule and for exploring issues of identity and totalitarianism.
sentences.zh: 他因描绘共产主义统治下中欧地区的压迫以及探讨身份认同和极权主义问题而闻名于世。

sentences.en: His writings were banned in communist Czechoslovakia, and he went into exile in France in 1975.
sentences.zh: 他的作品在当时的共产主义捷克斯洛伐克遭到禁售，并于1975年流亡法国。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了网罗了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党便陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时甚至扣人心弦的权力斗争之中。

sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·科尼格（Sarah Koenig）主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述那些试图维持自身影响力却最终失控的人的故事。
